title.raw: 卷112下 靈徵志八下 Volume 112b Treatise 8: The Spiritual World 2

sentences.zh: 魏氏世居幽朔，至獻帝世，有神人言應南遷，於是傳位於子聖武帝，命令南徙，山谷阻絕，仍欲止焉。

translations.literal: The Wei clan had long dwelt in You and Shuo; by the time of Emperor Xian, a divine man said they ought to migrate south, whereupon the throne was passed to his son Emperor Shengwu, who ordered a southward move; though ravines and mountains blocked the way, they still wished to halt.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei had long lived in the northern frontier region of You and Shuo. In the reign of Emperor Xian, a divine being declared that they should move south. The throne was then transferred to his son Emperor Shengwu, who commanded a migration southward; though ravines and mountains cut off the route, they still meant to stop there.

sentences.zh: 復有神獸，其形似馬，其聲類牛，先行導引，積年乃出。

translations.literal: Again there was a divine beast: its form resembled a horse and its voice was like an ox; it went ahead as guide, and only after many years did they emerge.
translations.idiomatic: A divine beast appeared—shaped like a horse, sounding like an ox—that marched ahead to lead them; only after many years did the clan break out.

sentences.zh: 始居匈奴之故地。

translations.literal: They first settled in the former lands of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: They first established themselves in the old territory of the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 高祖延興元年十一月，肆州秀容民獲麟以獻。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Yanxing 1 under Emperor Gaozu, a commoner of Xiurong in Si Prefecture captured a qilin and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Yanxing 1, a resident of Xiurong in Si Prefecture captured a qilin and sent it in as tribute.

sentences.zh: 王者不刳胎剖卵則至。

translations.literal: When a king does not cut open wombs or split eggs, [it] arrives.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler does not harm the unborn, the qilin appears.

sentences.zh: 世祖神䴥三年七月，冀州獻白龜。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Shenlu 3 under Emperor Shizu, Ji Prefecture presented a white tortoise.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Shenlu 3, Ji Prefecture sent in a white tortoise as tribute.

sentences.zh: 王者不私人以官，尊耆任舊，無偏黨之應。

translations.literal: When a king does not favor persons with offices, honors the aged and employs the old—[this is] the response to freedom from faction.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler appoints by merit rather than private favor, honors the elderly, and employs veterans without partisan bias, this omen responds.

sentences.zh: 高宗興安二年六月，營州送大龜。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Xing'an 2 under Emperor Gaozong, Ying Prefecture sent in a great tortoise.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Xing'an 2, Ying Prefecture forwarded a great tortoise to the court.

sentences.zh: 高祖延興元年十二月，徐州竹邑戍士邢德於彭城南一百二十里，得蓍一株，四十九枝，下掘得大龜獻之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of Yanxing 1 under Emperor Gaozu, Xing De, a garrison soldier of Zhuyi in Xu Prefecture, at a place one hundred twenty li south of Pengcheng obtained one stalk of yarrow of forty-nine branches; digging below, he obtained a great tortoise and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Yanxing 1, Xing De, a garrison soldier of Zhuyi in Xu Prefecture, one hundred twenty li south of Pengcheng found a yarrow plant of forty-nine stalks; digging beneath it he uncovered a great tortoise and presented both to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「龜蓍與經文相合，所謂靈物也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The tortoise and yarrow stalk accord with the classic texts—what are called numinous things.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "The tortoise and yarrow match the scriptures—they are what are called numinous creatures.

sentences.zh: 德可賜爵五等。」

translations.literal: De may be granted the fifth rank of nobility."
translations.idiomatic: De may be granted the fifth rank of nobility."

sentences.zh: 三年六月，京師獲大龜。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year, the capital obtained a great tortoise.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year, a great tortoise was captured at the capital.

sentences.zh: 肅宗神龜元年二月，獲龜於九龍殿靈芝池，大赦改元。

translations.literal: In the second month of Shengui 1 under Emperor Suzong, a tortoise was obtained at the Spirit Mushroom Pool of the Hall of Nine Dragons; a general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign title changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Shengui 1, a tortoise was found in the Spirit Mushroom Pool at the Hall of Nine Dragons; a general amnesty was declared and the era name changed.

sentences.zh: 孝靜武定三年十月，有司奏南兗州陳留郡民賈興達於家庭得毛龜一。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of Wuding 3 under Emperor Xiaojing, the responsible officials memorialized that Jia Xingda, a commoner of Chenliu Commandery in Southern Yan Prefecture, obtained one hairy tortoise at his home.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Wuding 3, the authorities reported that Jia Xingda, a commoner of Chenliu in Southern Yan Prefecture, had found a hairy tortoise in his household.

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Shenlu 3 under Emperor Shizu, Ji Prefecture presented a white tortoise.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Shenlu 3, Ji Prefecture sent in a white tortoise as tribute.

translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year, a great tortoise was captured at the capital.

sentences.zh: 天平四年八月，有巨象至於南兗州，碭郡民陳天愛以告，送京師，大赦改年。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Tianping, a huge elephant came to Southern Yan Prefecture; a commoner of Dang Commandery, Chen Tian'ai, reported it; it was sent to the capital and a general amnesty was proclaimed with a change of era.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Tianping 4, an enormous elephant arrived in Southern Yan Prefecture; Chen Tian'ai, a commoner of Dang Commandery, reported it; it was sent to the capital, a general amnesty was proclaimed, and the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 王者自養有節則至。

translations.literal: When a king moderates his own nourishment, [it] arrives.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler keeps his own consumption within bounds, such creatures appear.

sentences.zh: 高祖太和二年十一月，徐州獻黑狐。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Taihe 2 under Emperor Gaozu, Xu Prefecture presented a black fox.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Taihe 2, Xu Prefecture sent in a black fox as tribute.

sentences.zh: 周成王時，治致太平而黑狐見。

translations.literal: In the time of King Cheng of Zhou, governance reached great peace and a black fox appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of King Cheng of Zhou, order reached great peace and a black fox was seen.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，獲白狐。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, a white fox was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year, a white fox was captured.

sentences.zh: 王者仁智則至。

translations.literal: When a king is benevolent and wise, [it] arrives.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler is benevolent and wise, it appears.

sentences.zh: 六月，撫冥獲白狐以獻。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Fuming obtained a white fox and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, a white fox was captured at Fuming and sent in as tribute.

sentences.zh: 八年六月，徐州獲黑狐以獻。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eighth year, Xu Prefecture obtained a black fox and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eighth year, Xu Prefecture captured a black fox and presented it.

sentences.zh: 十年三月，冀州獲九尾狐以獻。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year, Ji Prefecture obtained a nine-tailed fox and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the tenth year, Ji Prefecture captured a nine-tailed fox and sent it in as tribute.

sentences.zh: 王者六合一統則見。

translations.literal: When a king unifies the six directions, [it] is seen.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler unifies all under Heaven, it is seen.

sentences.zh: 周文王時，東夷歸之。

translations.literal: In the time of King Wen of Zhou, the eastern Yi submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of King Wen of Zhou, the eastern Yi came to submit.

sentences.zh: 曰，王者不傾於色則至德至，鳥獸亦至。

translations.literal: It is said: when a king is not swayed by beauty, supreme virtue arrives and birds and beasts also come.
translations.idiomatic: It is said: when a ruler is not led astray by sensual pleasure, supreme virtue arrives and birds and beasts come as well.

sentences.zh: 十一年十一月，冀州獲九尾狐以獻。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the eleventh year, Ji Prefecture obtained a nine-tailed fox and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the eleventh year, Ji Prefecture captured a nine-tailed fox and sent it in as tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十三年正月，司州、河州各獻白狐狸。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-third year, Si Prefecture and He Prefecture each presented white foxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-third year, Si Prefecture and He Prefecture each sent in white foxes as tribute.

sentences.zh: 十九年六月，司州平陽郡獲白狐以獻。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the nineteenth year, Pingyang Commandery in Si Prefecture obtained a white fox and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the nineteenth year, Pingyang Commandery in Si Prefecture captured a white fox and presented it.

sentences.zh: 世宗景明三年二月，河州獻白狐。

translations.literal: In the second month of Jingming 3 under Emperor Shizong, He Prefecture presented a white fox.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Jingming 3, He Prefecture sent in a white fox as tribute.

sentences.zh: 永平三年十月，白狐見於汲郡。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of Yongping 3, a white fox was seen at Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yongping 3, a white fox appeared in Ji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 延昌四年四月，兗州獻白狐。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Yanchang 4, Yan Prefecture presented a white fox.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yanchang 4, Yan Prefecture sent in a white fox as tribute.

sentences.zh: 九月，相州獻白狐。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Xiang Prefecture presented a white fox.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Xiang Prefecture sent in a white fox as tribute.

sentences.zh: 閏月，汾州獻白狐二。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Fen Prefecture presented two white foxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Fen Prefecture sent in two white foxes as tribute.

sentences.zh: 肅宗正光二年三月，南青州獻白狐二。

translations.literal: In the third month of Zhenguang 2 under Emperor Suzong, Southern Qing Prefecture presented two white foxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Zhenguang 2, Southern Qing Prefecture sent in two white foxes as tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，平陽郡獻白狐。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year, Pingyang Commandery presented a white fox.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year, Pingyang Commandery sent in a white fox as tribute.

sentences.zh: 八月，光州獻九尾狐。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Guang Prefecture presented a nine-tailed fox.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Guang Prefecture sent in a nine-tailed fox as tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，平陽郡獻白狐。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, Pingyang Commandery presented a white fox.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year, Pingyang Commandery sent in a white fox as tribute.

sentences.zh: 孝靜天平四年四月，西兗州獻白狐；

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Tianping 4 under Emperor Xiaojing, Western Yan Prefecture presented a white fox;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Tianping 4, Western Yan Prefecture sent in a white fox as tribute;

sentences.zh: 七月，光州獻九尾狐。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Guang Prefecture presented a nine-tailed fox.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Guang Prefecture sent in a nine-tailed fox as tribute.

sentences.zh: 元象元年四月，光州獻九尾狐。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Yuanxiang 1, Guang Prefecture presented a nine-tailed fox.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yuanxiang 1, Guang Prefecture sent in a nine-tailed fox as tribute.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，光州獻九尾狐。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, Guang Prefecture presented a nine-tailed fox.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year, Guang Prefecture sent in a nine-tailed fox as tribute.

sentences.zh: 興和三年五月，司州獻九尾狐。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of Xinghe 3, Si Prefecture presented a nine-tailed fox.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Xinghe 3, Si Prefecture sent in a nine-tailed fox as tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二月，魏郡獻白狐。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Wei Commandery presented a white fox.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Wei Commandery sent in a white fox as tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，瀛州獻白狐二。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Ying Prefecture presented two white foxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Ying Prefecture sent in two white foxes as tribute.

sentences.zh: 武定元年七月，幽州獲白狐，以獻上。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Wuding 1, You Prefecture obtained a white fox and presented it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Wuding 1, You Prefecture captured a white fox and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，瀛州獻白狐，二牡一牝。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year, Ying Prefecture presented white foxes, two males and one female.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year, Ying Prefecture sent in white foxes—two males and one female.

sentences.zh: 九月，西兗州獻白狐。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Western Yan Prefecture presented a white fox.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Western Yan Prefecture sent in a white fox as tribute.

sentences.zh: 太和二年十一月辛未，泰州獻五色狗。

translations.literal: On the xinwei day of the eleventh month of Taihe 2, Tai Prefecture presented a five-colored dog.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day of the eleventh month of Taihe 2, Tai Prefecture sent in a five-colored dog.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，齊州獻五色狗，其五色如畫。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year, Qi Prefecture presented a five-colored dog; its five colors were as if painted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year, Qi Prefecture sent in a five-colored dog whose hues were like painted work.

sentences.zh: 太祖天興四年五月，魏郡斥丘縣獲白鹿。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of Tianxing 4 under Emperor Taizu, Chiqiu County in Wei Commandery obtained a white deer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tianxing 4, Chiqiu County in Wei Commandery captured a white deer.

sentences.zh: 王者惠及下則至。

translations.literal: When a king's bounty reaches those below, [it] arrives.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler's grace reaches those below, it appears.

sentences.zh: 太宗永興四年九月，建興郡獻白鹿。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of Yongxing 4 under Emperor Taizong, Jianxing Commandery presented a white deer.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Yongxing 4, Jianxing Commandery sent in a white deer as tribute.

sentences.zh: 世祖神䴥元年二月，定州獲白䴥，白䴥鹿又見於樂陵，[1]因以改元。

translations.literal: In the second month of Shenlu 1 under Emperor Shizu, Ding Prefecture obtained a white stag; a white stag was also seen at Leling, [1] and the reign title was changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Shenlu 1, Ding Prefecture captured a white stag, and another white stag appeared at Leling; [1] the era name was changed on this account.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，白鹿見於代郡倒剌山。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, a white deer was seen at Daoci Mountain in Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year, a white deer appeared on Daoci Mountain in Dai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 太延四年十二月，相州獻白鹿。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of Taiyan 4, Xiang Prefecture presented a white deer.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Taiyan 4, Xiang Prefecture sent in a white deer as tribute.

sentences.zh: 真君八年五月，洛州送白鹿。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Zhenjun, Luo Prefecture sent in a white deer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Zhenjun, Luo Prefecture forwarded a white deer to the court.

sentences.zh: 高宗太安二年十月，白鹿見於京師西苑。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of Tai'an 2 under Emperor Gaozong, a white deer was seen at the Western Park of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Tai'an 2, a white deer appeared in the Western Park at the capital.

sentences.zh: 三月，白鹿見於青州。

translations.literal: In the third month, a white deer was seen at Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, a white deer appeared in Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，南豫州獻白鹿。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, Southern Yu Prefecture presented a white deer.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year, Southern Yu Prefecture sent in a white deer as tribute.

sentences.zh: 十九年七月，司州獲白鹿、麑以獻。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the nineteenth year, Si Prefecture obtained a white deer and fawn and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the nineteenth year, Si Prefecture captured a white deer and fawn and presented them.

sentences.zh: 二十年六月，司州獻白鹿。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twentieth year, Si Prefecture presented a white deer.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twentieth year, Si Prefecture sent in a white deer as tribute.

sentences.zh: 世宗景明元年四月，荊州獻白鹿。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Jingming 1 under Emperor Shizong, Jing Prefecture presented a white deer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Jingming 1, Jing Prefecture sent in a white deer as tribute.

sentences.zh: 永平四年八月，平州獻白鹿。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Yongping 4, Ping Prefecture presented a white deer.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Yongping 4, Ping Prefecture sent in a white deer as tribute.

sentences.zh: 延昌二年五月，齊州獻白鹿。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of Yanchang 2, Qi Prefecture presented a white deer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Yanchang 2, Qi Prefecture sent in a white deer as tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，司州獻白鹿。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year, Si Prefecture presented a white deer.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year, Si Prefecture sent in a white deer as tribute.

sentences.zh: 肅宗熙平元年五月，濟州獻白鹿。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of Xiping 1 under Emperor Suzong, Ji Prefecture presented a white deer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Xiping 1, Ji Prefecture sent in a white deer as tribute.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，司州獻白鹿。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year, Si Prefecture presented a white deer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year, Si Prefecture sent in a white deer as tribute.

sentences.zh: 神龜二年六月，徐州獻白鹿。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Shengui 2, Xu Prefecture presented a white deer.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Shengui 2, Xu Prefecture sent in a white deer as tribute.

sentences.zh: 武定元年六月，兗州獻白鹿。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Wuding 1, Yan Prefecture presented a white deer.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Wuding 1, Yan Prefecture sent in a white deer as tribute.

sentences.zh: 太祖登國六年十二月，上獵，親獲鹿一角。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Dengguo under Emperor Taizu, the emperor went hunting and personally obtained a deer with one horn.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Dengguo, the emperor went on a hunt and personally took a one-horned deer.

sentences.zh: 召問羣臣，皆曰：「鹿當二角，今一，是諸國將并之應也。」

translations.literal: He summoned and questioned the assembled ministers; all said: "A deer should have two horns; now there is one—this is the omen that the various states will be annexed."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the ministers and asked them; all said, "A deer should have two horns; now there is only one—this is an omen that the various states will be annexed."

sentences.zh: 太祖天興四年春，新興太守上言：「晉昌民賈相，昔年二十二，為雁門郡吏，入句注西陘，見一老父，謂相曰：『自今以後四十二年當有聖人出於北方。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Tianxing under Emperor Taizu, the Administrator of Xinxing memorialized: "The commoner Jia Xiang of Jinchang, then aged twenty-two, was once a clerk of Yanmen Commandery; entering the western pass of Gouzhu, he saw an old man who said to Xiang: 'From now, in forty-two years a sage will arise in the north.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Tianxing 4, the Administrator of Xinxing reported: "Jia Xiang, a commoner of Jinchang, was twenty-two when he served as a clerk in Yanmen Commandery. Entering the western pass at Gouzhu, he met an old man who told him, 'Within forty-two years a sage will emerge from the north.

sentences.zh: 時當大樂，子孫永長，吾不及見之。』

translations.literal: Then there will be great rejoicing; your descendants will endure long—I shall not live to see it.
translations.idiomatic: There will be great peace and your line will flourish; I shall not live to see it.

sentences.zh: 言終而過。

translations.literal: Having spoken, he passed on.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished speaking, he went on his way.

sentences.zh: 相顧視之，父老化為石人。

translations.literal: Xiang looked back and the old man had turned into a stone man.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang turned to look: the old man had become a stone figure.

sentences.zh: 相今七十。

translations.literal: Xiang is now seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang is now seventy years old.

sentences.zh: 下檢石人見存。

translations.literal: On inspection below, the stone man still stands.
translations.idiomatic: On examination the stone figure is still there.

sentences.zh: 至帝破慕容寶之歲，四十二年。」

translations.literal: In the year the emperor defeated Murong Bao, it was exactly forty-two years."

sentences.zh: 真君五年二月，張掖郡上言：「往曹氏之世，丘池縣大柳谷山石表龍馬之形，石馬脊文曰『大討曹』，而晉氏代魏。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year of Zhenjun, Zhangye Commandery reported: "In the age of the Cao house, at Daliugu in Qiuchi County, a mountain stone bore the form of a dragon-horse; on the stone horse's back was the inscription 'Great chastisement of Cao,' and the Jin house replaced Wei.

sentences.zh: 今石文記國家祖宗諱，著受命之符。」

translations.literal: Now the stone writing records the taboo names of our state's ancestors, displaying the token of Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 初上封太平王，天文圖錄又授「太平真君」之號，與石文相應。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as Prince of Peace; the astronomical registers also granted the title "True Lord of Peace," matching the stone writing.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was enfeoffed as Prince of Peace; the astronomical registers also granted the title "True Lord of Peace," matching the stone writing.

sentences.zh: 太宗名諱之後，有一人象，攜一小兒。

sentences.zh: 見者皆曰：「上愛皇孫，提攜臥起，不離左右，此即上象靈契，真天授也。」

translations.idiomatic: All who saw it said: "The emperor loves the imperial grandson, raising and tending him, never leaving his side—this is the heavenly image of spiritual accord, a true gift of Heaven."

translations.literal: Thereupon Guard General, Prince of Le'an Fan, Assistant General Who Supports the State, Prince of Jianning Chong, General Who Conquers the West, Prince of Changshan Su, and General Who Conquers the South, Prince of Hengnong Xi Jin submitted: "We have heard that the rise of emperors and kings always carries a token of mandate, enabling them to align the three powers and establish the supreme norm; the glories of the Three and Five were alike in this.

sentences.zh: 伏羲有河圖、八卦，夏禹有洛書、九疇，至乃神功播於往古，聖跡顯於來世。

translations.literal: Fuxi had the Yellow River Chart and the Eight Trigrams; Yu of Xia had the Luo Writ and the Nine Categories; thus divine achievements were spread abroad in antiquity and sage traces made manifest for later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxi received the River Chart and the Eight Trigrams; Yu of Xia received the Luo Writ and the Nine Categories—so that sacred deeds were known in the past and sage footprints shown to posterity.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下德合乾坤，明並日月，固天縱聖，應運挺生，上靈垂顧，徵善備集。

translations.literal: We consider that Your Majesty's virtue matches Heaven and Earth and your brilliance equals sun and moon; Heaven-born sagacity, you arose in response to the age; the upper spirits look down and every auspicious sign gathers.
translations.idiomatic: We consider that Your Majesty's virtue matches Heaven and Earth and your brilliance equals sun and moon; Heaven-born sagacity, you arose in response to the age; the upper spirits look down and every auspicious sign gathers.

sentences.zh: 是以始光元年經天師奉天文圖錄，授『太平真君』之號。

translations.literal: Thus in the first year of Shiguang the Celestial Master presented the astronomical registers, conferring the title 'True Lord of Peace.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in the first year of Shiguang the Celestial Master presented the astronomical registers, conferring the title 'True Lord of Peace.

sentences.zh: 陛下深執虛沖，歷年乃受。

translations.literal: Your Majesty deeply held to emptiness and humility and accepted only after years.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty deeply held to emptiness and humility and accepted only after years.

sentences.zh: 精誠感於靈物，信惠協於天人，用能威加四海，澤流宇內，溥天率土，無思不服。

translations.literal: Sincerity moved numinous things; trust and kindness harmonized Heaven and man; thus your might extended over the four seas and your bounty flowed through the realm; all under Heaven within the four seas none failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Sincerity moved numinous things; trust and kindness harmonized Heaven and man; thus your might extended over the four seas and your bounty flowed through the realm; all under Heaven within the four seas none failed to submit.

sentences.zh: 今張掖郡列言：丘池縣大柳谷山大石有青質白章，間成文字，記國家祖宗之諱，著受命歷數之符。

translations.literal: Now Zhangye Commandery reports: at Daliugu in Qiuchi County great stones of green substance and white markings bear writing between them, recording the taboo names of the state's ancestors and displaying the token of the mandate and the span of rule.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhangye Commandery reports: at Daliugu in Qiuchi County great stones of green substance and white markings bear writing between them, recording the taboo names of the state's ancestors and displaying the token of the mandate and the span of rule.

sentences.zh: 王公已下，羣司百辟，覩此圖文，莫不感動，僉曰：自古以來，禎祥之驗，未有今日之煥炳也。

translations.literal: From princes and dukes down through every office, all who beheld this script were moved; unanimously they said: since antiquity the verification of auspicious signs has never blazed as brightly as today.
translations.idiomatic: From princes and dukes down through every office, all who beheld this script were moved; unanimously they said: since antiquity the verification of auspicious signs has never blazed as brightly as today.

sentences.zh: 斯乃上靈降命，國家無窮之徵也。

translations.literal: This is the highest spirits descending mandate—the omen of the state's boundless fortune.
translations.idiomatic: This is the highest spirits descending mandate—the omen of the state's boundless fortune.

sentences.zh: 臣等幸遭盛化，沐浴光寵，無以對揚天休，增廣天地，謹與羣臣參議，宜以石文之徵，宣告四海，令方外僭竊知天命有歸。」

translations.literal: We are fortunate to encounter this great transformation, bathed in glory and favor; having no means to respond to Heaven's blessing and enlarge Heaven and Earth, we respectfully deliberated with the assembled ministers: the stone inscription should be proclaimed throughout the four seas, so that pretenders beyond our borders know that Heaven's mandate has a rightful home."
translations.idiomatic: We are fortunate to encounter this great transformation, bathed in glory and favor; having no means to respond to Heaven's blessing and enlarge Heaven and Earth, we respectfully deliberated with the assembled ministers: the stone inscription should be proclaimed throughout the four seas, so that pretenders beyond our borders know that Heaven's mandate has a rightful home."

sentences.zh: 制曰：「此天地況施，乃先祖父之遺徵，豈朕一人所能獨致。

translations.literal: An edict said: "This is Heaven and Earth's generous gift—the legacy sign of our forefathers; how could I alone have brought it about?
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "This is Heaven and Earth's generous gift—the legacy sign of our forefathers; how could I alone have brought it about?

sentences.zh: 可如所奏。」

translations.literal: Let it be done as memorialized."
translations.idiomatic: Let it be done as memorialized."

sentences.zh: 顯祖皇興三年六月，尉元表：「臣於彭城遣別將以八日至睢口邀賊將陳顯達，[5]有戰士於營外五里芻牧，見一白頭翁，乘白馬，將軍，[6]呼之語，稱：『至十八日辰必來到此，語汝將軍，領眾從東北臨入，我當驅賊令走。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Huangxing under Emperor Xianzu, Wei Yuan memorialized: "Your servant, at Pengcheng, sent a separate commander who in eight days reached Suikou to intercept the rebel general Chen Xianda; [5] a soldier five li outside camp gathering fodder saw a white-haired old man riding a white horse, a general, [6] called to him and spoke, saying: 'On the eighteenth day at the chen hour I shall certainly come here; tell your general to lead his troops in from the northeast—I shall drive the rebels to flee.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Huangxing 3, Wei Yuan reported: "At Pengcheng I sent a detached commander who reached Suikou in eight days to intercept Chen Xianda. [5] A forager five li from camp saw a white-haired man on a white horse, a commander, [6] who called to him and said: 'On the eighteenth at chen hour I will come; tell your general to enter from the northeast—I will put the rebels to flight.

sentences.zh: 申時，賊必大破，宿豫、淮陽皆克無疑。

translations.literal: At the shen hour the rebels will surely suffer great defeat; Suyu and Huaiyang will both be taken without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: At the shen hour the rebels will be utterly defeated; Suyu and Huaiyang will fall without doubt.

sentences.zh: 我當與汝國家淮畔為斷，下邳城我當驅出，[7]不勞兵力。』

translations.literal: I shall make the Huai bank a boundary for your state; I shall drive Xiapi city out, [7] without troubling your forces."
translations.idiomatic: I shall make the Huai bank a boundary for your state; I shall drive Xiapi city out, [7] without troubling your forces."

sentences.zh: 後十日，此人復於彭城南戲馬臺東二里見白頭翁，亦乘白馬，從東北來，呼此人謂曰：『我與東海、四瀆、太山、北嶽神共行淮北，助汝二將蕩除已定。

translations.literal: Ten days later this man again saw the white-haired old man east of Ximatai, two li south of Pengcheng, also riding a white horse, coming from the northeast; he called to this man and said: "I am traveling north of the Huai together with the gods of the Eastern Sea, the Four Waterways, Mount Tai, and the Northern Peak to help your two generals sweep the enemy away—it is already settled.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later this man again saw the white-haired old man east of Ximatai, two li south of Pengcheng, also riding a white horse, coming from the northeast; he called to this man and said: "I am traveling north of the Huai together with the gods of the Eastern Sea, the Four Waterways, Mount Tai, and the Northern Peak to help your two generals sweep the enemy away—it is already settled.

sentences.zh: 汝上下喜不？』

translations.literal: Are you high and low not rejoicing?"
translations.idiomatic: Are you high and low not rejoicing?"

sentences.zh: 因忽然不見。」

translations.literal: Then suddenly he vanished."
translations.idiomatic: Then suddenly he vanished."

sentences.zh: 詔元於老人前後見所，為壇表記之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yuan to erect altars and record the places where the old man had appeared before and after.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed Yuan to build altars and mark where the old man had appeared before and after.

sentences.zh: 肅宗孝昌二年十月，揚州刺史李憲表云：「門下督周伏興以去七月患假還家，至十一日夜夢渡肥水，行至草堂寺南，遙見七人，一人乘馬著朱衣，籠冠，六人從後。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Xiaochang under Emperor Suzong, Li Xian, Inspector of Yangzhou, memorialized: "Gate Officer Zhou Fuxing, on sick leave returning home last seventh month, on the night of the eleventh dreamed he crossed the Fei River; reaching south of Caotang Temple he saw seven men from afar—one riding a horse in vermilion robes with a caged cap, six following behind.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Xiaochang 2, Li Xian, inspector of Yangzhou, reported: "Gate Officer Zhou Fuxing, on sick leave at home since the seventh month, dreamed on the night of the eleventh that he crossed the Fei River. South of Caotang Temple he saw seven men in the distance—one on horseback in vermilion robes with a tall cap, six walking behind.

sentences.zh: 興路左而立，至便再拜。

translations.literal: Xing stood to the roadside; when they arrived he bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Xing stood by the road; when they reached him he bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 問興何人。

translations.literal: They asked who Xing was.
translations.idiomatic: They asked his name.

sentences.zh: 興對曰：『李公門下督，暫使硤石。』

translations.literal: Xing replied: 'A gate officer of Lord Li, temporarily sent to Qiaoshi.'
translations.idiomatic: Xing answered: 'I am a gate officer of Lord Li, temporarily sent to Qiaoshi.'

sentences.zh: 其人語興：『君可回，我是孝文皇帝中書舍人，遣語李憲，勿憂賊堰，此月破矣。』

translations.literal: The man said to Xing: 'You may return—I am a Secretariat Gentleman of Emperor Xiaowen, sent to tell Li Xian not to worry about the enemy dam; this month it will be broken.'
translations.idiomatic: He told Xing: 'Go back—I am a secretariat gentleman of Emperor Xiaowen, sent to tell Li Xian not to fear the enemy dam; it will break this month.'

sentences.zh: 興行兩步，錄興姓字，令興速白。

translations.literal: Xing walked two steps; they recorded Xing's surname and given name and ordered Xing to report quickly.
translations.idiomatic: After two steps they wrote down his name and told him to report at once.

sentences.zh: 興寤，曉遂還城，具言夢狀。

translations.literal: Xing awoke; at dawn he returned to the city and fully reported the dream.
translations.idiomatic: Xing woke; at dawn he returned to the city and reported the dream in full.

sentences.zh: 七月二十七日，堰破。」

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month, the dam was broken."
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh of the seventh month the dam broke."

sentences.zh: 世祖延和三年三月，樂安王範獲玉璽一，文曰「皇帝璽」以獻。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Yanhe under Emperor Shizu, Prince of Le'an Fan obtained one jade seal, inscribed "Imperial Seal" and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Yanhe under Emperor Shizu, Prince of Le'an Fan captured one jade seal, inscribed "Imperial Seal" and sent in it as tribute.

sentences.zh: 太延元年，自三月不雨至六月，使有司遍請羣神，數日，大雨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiyan, from the third month without rain until the sixth month, the court sent officials to invoke the gods everywhere; within days, great rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyan 1, drought lasted from the third month to the sixth; officials were sent to pray to the gods throughout the realm, and within days heavy rain fell.

sentences.zh: 是日，有婦人持一玉印至潞縣侯孫家賣之。

translations.literal: On that day, a woman brought a jade seal to Marquis Sun's house in Lu County to sell it.
translations.idiomatic: That day a woman came to Marquis Sun's residence in Lu County offering a jade seal for sale.

sentences.zh: 孫家得印，奇之，求訪婦人，莫知所在。

translations.literal: The Sun family obtained the seal and marveled at it; they sought the woman, but no one knew where she had gone.
translations.idiomatic: The Sun family obtained the seal and marveled at it; they sought the woman, but no one knew where she had gone.

sentences.zh: 其文曰：「旱疫平。」

translations.literal: Its inscription read: "Drought and pestilence pacified."
translations.idiomatic: Its inscription read: "Drought and pestilence pacified."

sentences.zh: 寇天師曰：「龍文紐書云，此神中三字印也。」

translations.literal: Master Kou the Celestial Master said: "The dragon-script seal writing states this is the three-character seal of the spirits."
translations.idiomatic: Celestial Master Kou said: "The dragon-script seal tradition identifies this as the spirits' three-character seal."

sentences.zh: 高宗和平三年四月，河內人張超於壞樓所城北故佛圖處獲玉印以獻。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Heping 3 under Emperor Gaozong, Zhang Chao of Henei obtained a jade seal at the old Buddha shrine north of the city wall at Huailou and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Heping 3, Zhang Chao of Henei found a jade seal at the ruined Buddha site north of Huailou city and sent it in as tribute.

sentences.zh: [8]印方二寸，其文曰：「富樂日昌，永保無疆，福祿日臻，長享萬年。」

translations.literal: [8] The seal was two inches square; its text read: "Wealth and joy daily flourish; forever secure without limit; fortune and salary daily advance; long enjoy ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: [8] The seal was two inches square; its text read: "Wealth and joy daily flourish; forever secure without limit; fortune and salary daily advance; long enjoy ten thousand years."

sentences.zh: 玉色光潤，模制精巧，百僚咸曰：「神明所授，非人為也。」

translations.literal: Its jade hue was lustrous and its mold-work exquisitely fine. All officials said: "Granted by the spirits—not made by human hands."
translations.idiomatic: Its jade hue was lustrous and its mold-work exquisitely fine. All officials said: "Granted by the spirits—not made by human hands."

sentences.zh: 詔天下大酺三日。

translations.literal: An edict proclaimed a grand feast throughout the realm for three days.
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed a grand feast throughout the realm for three days.

sentences.zh: 高祖承明元年八月，上谷郡民獻玉印，上有蛟龍文。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Chengming 1 under Emperor Gaozu, commoners of Shanggu Commandery presented a jade seal bearing the pattern of a flood dragon.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Chengming 1, Shanggu commoners sent in a jade seal marked with a flood-dragon design.

sentences.zh: 太和元年三月，武川鎮獻玉印，青質素文，其文曰「太昌」。

translations.literal: In the third month of Taihe 1, Wuchuan Garrison presented a jade seal of green substance with plain markings; its inscription read "Taichang."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Taihe 1, Wuchuan Garrison sent in a green jade seal with plain text reading "Taichang."

sentences.zh: 六月，雍州獻玉印。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Yong Province presented jade seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Yong Province sent in jade seal as tribute.

sentences.zh: 是月，長安鎮獻玉印一，上有龜紐，下有文字，色甚鮮白，有殊常玉。

translations.literal: In the same month, Chang'an Garrison presented one jade seal with a tortoise knob above and writing below; its color was very bright white, unlike ordinary jade.
translations.idiomatic: In the same month, Chang'an Garrison sent in a jade seal with a tortoise knob and inscription, brilliantly white and unlike common jade.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，定州鉅鹿民獻玉印一方，七分，上有文字。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year, commoners of Julu in Ding Prefecture presented one square jade seal, seven fen in size, with writing on it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year, Julu in Ding Prefecture sent in a square jade seal seven fen across, bearing an inscription.

sentences.zh: 世宗永平元年四月，瀛州民獲玉璧、玉印各一以獻。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Yongping 1 under Emperor Shizong, commoners of Ying Prefecture obtained one jade bi and one jade seal and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yongping 1, Ying Prefecture commoners captured a jade bi and a jade seal and sent them in as tribute.

sentences.zh: 肅宗熙平二年十一月，京師仍獲玉璽二。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Xiping 2 under Emperor Suzong, the capital again obtained two jade seals.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Xiping 2, two more jade seals were captured at the capital.

sentences.zh: 孝靜興和三年二月，東郡白馬縣民獻玉印一。

translations.literal: In the second month of Xinghe 3 under Emperor Xiaojing, commoners of Baima County in Dong Commandery presented one jade seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Xinghe 3, Baima County in Dong Commandery sent in one jade seal as tribute.

sentences.zh: 太宗永興三年十二月，北塞候人獲玉板二以獻。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of Yongxing 3 under Emperor Taizong, a northern frontier sentry obtained two jade tablets and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Yongxing 3, a northern border sentry captured two jade tablets and sent them in as tribute.

sentences.zh: 王者慈仁則見。

translations.literal: When a king is merciful and benevolent, [it] is seen.
translations.idiomatic: When a king is merciful and benevolent, it is seen.

sentences.zh: 孝靜天平二年二月，員外散騎常侍穆禮得玉板一，廣三寸，長尺五寸，頭有兩孔以獻。

translations.literal: In the second month of Tianping 2 under Emperor Xiaojing, Mu Li, Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, obtained one jade tablet three cun wide and one foot five cun long, with two holes at the head, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tianping 2, Mu Li, supernumerary attendant of the scattered cavalry, presented a jade tablet three by fifteen cun with two holes at the top.

sentences.zh: 高祖承明元年九月，京兆民獻青玉璧一雙，文色炳煥。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of Chengming 1 under Emperor Gaozu, Jingzhao commoners presented one pair of green jade bi, their pattern and color brilliant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Chengming 1, Jingzhao commoners sent in a pair of green jade bi of brilliant hue and design.

sentences.zh: 王者賢良美德則至。

translations.literal: When a king possesses worthy virtue and beautiful conduct, [it] arrives.
translations.idiomatic: When a king possesses worthy virtue and beautiful conduct, it appears.

sentences.zh: 肅宗正光三年六月，并州靜林寺僧在陽邑城西橡谷掘藥，得玉璧五，珪十，印一，玉柱一，玉蓋一，並以獻。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Zhenguang 3 under Emperor Suzong, a monk of Jinglin Monastery in Bing Prefecture, digging medicine in Oak Valley west of Yangyi city, obtained five jade bi, ten jade tablets, one seal, one jade column, and one jade canopy, and presented them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Zhenguang 3, a monk of Jinglin Monastery in Bing Prefecture found five jade bi, ten tablets, a seal, a column, and a canopy in Oak Valley west of Yangyi and presented them all.

sentences.zh: 高祖太和五年六月，上邽鎮將上言：「於鎮城西二百五十里射獵，於營南千水中得玉車釧三枚，二青一赤，制狀甚精。」

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Taihe under Emperor Gaozu, the garrison commander of Shanggui reported: "Two hundred fifty li west of the fort, while hunting, in the thousand streams south of camp three jade arm-rings were obtained—two green and one red—wrought with great refinement."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Taihe under Emperor Gaozu, the garrison commander of Shanggui reported: "Two hundred fifty li west of the fort, while hunting, in the thousand streams south of camp three jade arm-rings were obtained—two green and one red—wrought with great refinement."

sentences.zh: 孝靜興和四年七月，鄴縣民獻白玉一璞。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Xinghe 4 under Emperor Xiaojing, commoners of Ye County presented one piece of uncut white jade.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Xinghe 4, Ye County commoners sent in one uncut piece of white jade.

sentences.zh: 肅宗熙平二年正月，金出岐州橫水縣赤粟谷。

translations.literal: In the first month of Xiping 2 under Emperor Suzong, gold appeared in Red Millet Valley, Hengshui County, Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xiping 2, gold was found in Red Millet Valley, Hengshui County, Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太祖天興三年四月，有木連理，生於代郡天門關之路左。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Tianxing 3 under Emperor Taizu, intertwined trees grew to the left of the road at Tianmen Pass in Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Tianxing 3, conjoined trees appeared beside the road at Tianmen Pass in Dai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 王者德澤純洽，八方為一則生。

translations.literal: When a king's virtue and bounty are pure and harmonized and the eight directions are one, [it] grows.
translations.idiomatic: When a king's virtue and bounty are pure and harmonized and the eight directions are one, [it] grows.

sentences.zh: 八月，勃海上言脩縣、東光縣木連理各一。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Bohai reported that Xiuxian and Dongguang counties each had one instance of intertwined trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Bohai reported intertwined trees in Xiuxian and Dongguang counties, one in each.

sentences.zh: 十二月，豫州上言木連理生於河內之沁縣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Yu Prefecture reported that intertwined trees had grown in Qinshui County, Henei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Yu Prefecture reported intertwined trees growing in Qinshui County, Henei.

translations.literal: [lacuna]
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note 9.

sentences.zh: 四年春，河內郡木連理二。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, Henei Commandery had two instances of intertwined trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year, two intertwined trees appeared in Henei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 八月，魏郡上言內黃縣木連理。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Wei Commandery reported intertwined trees in Neihuang County.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Wei Commandery reported intertwined trees in Neihuang County.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰常元年十月，范陽郡上言木連理。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of Taichang 1 under Emperor Taizong, Fanyang Commandery reported intertwined trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Taichang 1, Fanyang Commandery reported intertwined trees.

sentences.zh: 十一月，常山郡上言木連理。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Changshan Commandery reported intertwined trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Changshan Commandery reported intertwined trees.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，勃海上言東光縣木連理。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, Bohai reported intertwined trees in Dongguang County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, Bohai reported intertwined trees in Dongguang County.

sentences.zh: 八月，廣寧郡上言木連理。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Guangning Commandery reported upward: intertwined trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Guangning Commandery reported upward: intertwined trees.

sentences.zh: 世祖神䴥四年九月，滎陽郡上言木連理。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Shenlu under Emperor Shizu, Xingyang Commandery reported upward: intertwined trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Shenlu under Emperor Shizu, Xingyang Commandery reported upward: intertwined trees.

sentences.zh: 延和二年三月，樓煩南山木連理。

translations.literal: In the third month of Yanhe 2, intertwined trees appeared on the southern mountain of Loufan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Yanhe 2, intertwined trees grew on Loufan's southern mountain.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，上谷郡上言木連理。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year, Shanggu Commandery reported upward: intertwined trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year, Shanggu Commandery reported upward: intertwined trees.

sentences.zh: 太延元年二月，魏郡上言木連理。

translations.literal: In the second month of Taiyan 1, Wei Commandery reported intertwined trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Taiyan 1, Wei Commandery reported intertwined trees.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，遼西上言木連理。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year, Liaoxi reported upward: intertwined trees.

sentences.zh: 定州獲白䴥白䴥鹿又見於樂陵 按「䴥」乃牡鹿，無須下着「鹿」字，疑下「䴥」或「鹿」字衍其一。

translations.literal: Ding Prefecture obtained a white stag; a white stag was also seen at Leling. Commentary: "Ji" denotes a male deer and need not be followed by the character "deer"; suspect one of the characters "ji" or "deer" below is redundant.
translations.idiomatic: Collation on Ding Prefecture white stag entries: the character for male deer need not be followed by "deer"; one character is likely redundant.

sentences.zh: 王者爵祿均則白雀至 百衲本「均」字空格，他本注「闕」字。

translations.literal: When a king's ranks and stipends are equal, the white sparrow arrives. The Bainapu edition leaves a blank for "equal"; other editions note "missing character."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: "equal" is blank in the Bainapu edition; other editions mark the character as missing.

sentences.zh: 今據宋書卷二九符瑞志下補。

translations.literal: Now supplemented according to Song Shu, Treatise on Portents, Part B.
translations.idiomatic: Now supplemented according to Song Shu, Treatise on Portents, Part B.

sentences.zh: 其文記昭成皇帝諱繼世四六天法平天下大安凡十四字 百衲、北、汲三本「帝」作「后」，南、殿、局三本作「帝」。

translations.literal: The writing records the taboo name of Emperor Zhaocheng: "Succession through generations, four-six; Heaven's law is level; all under Heaven great peace"—fourteen characters in all. Bainna, Northern, and Ji editions read "empress" for "emperor"; Southern, Palace, and Bureau editions read "emperor."
translations.idiomatic: The writing records the taboo name of Emperor Zhaocheng: "Succession through generations, four-six; Heaven's law is level; all under Heaven great peace"—fourteen characters in all. Bainna, Northern, and Ji editions read "empress" for "emperor"; Southern, Palace, and Bureau editions read "emperor."

sentences.zh: 殿本考證云「昭成帝諱什翼犍，今以『什翼犍』三字并下『繼世四六天法平天下大安』十一字合之，恰與十四字之數相符」。

translations.literal: The Palace edition's textual note states: "Emperor Zhaocheng's taboo name Sheyijian—combining the three characters with the eleven below 'Succession through generations, four-six; Heaven's law is level; all under Heaven great peace'—exactly matches fourteen characters."
translations.idiomatic: Palace edition note: Emperor Zhaocheng's taboo name Sheyijian, plus the eleven characters below, totals fourteen as required.

sentences.zh: 按考證說是，今從南、殿、局本。

translations.literal: The commentary is accepted; we follow the Southern, Palace, and Bureau editions.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary is accepted; we follow the Southern, Palace, and Bureau editions.

sentences.zh: 次記太宗明元皇帝諱長子二百二十年凡八字 百衲、北、汲、局四本「八」作「六」，南、殿本作「八」。

translations.literal: Next recorded the taboo name of Emperor Taizong, Emperor Mingyuan: "Eldest son, two hundred twenty years"—eight characters in all. Bainna, Northern, Ji, and Bureau editions read "six" for "eight"; Southern and Palace read "eight."
translations.idiomatic: Next recorded the taboo name of Emperor Taizong, Emperor Mingyuan: "Eldest son, two hundred twenty years"—eight characters in all. Bainna, Northern, Ji, and Bureau editions read "six" for "eight"; Southern and Palace read "eight."

sentences.zh: 殿本考證云：「明元帝諱嗣，今以『嗣』字并下『長子二百二十年』七字合之，則『六』字必係『八』字之訛。」

translations.literal: The Palace edition's note: "Emperor Mingyuan's taboo name Si—combining that character with the seven below 'Eldest son, two hundred twenty years'—shows the character 'eight' must be an error for 'six'."
translations.idiomatic: Palace edition note: Emperor Mingyuan's taboo Si plus seven following characters—eight should read six."

sentences.zh: 按考證說是，今從南、殿本。

translations.literal: The commentary is accepted; we follow the Southern and Palace editions.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary is accepted; we follow the Southern and Palace editions.

sentences.zh: 臣於彭城遣別將以八日至睢口邀賊將陳顯達 諸本「八日」作「八月」，冊府卷三九八

translations.literal: Your servant at Pengcheng sent a separate commander who in eight days [reached] Suikou to intercept the rebel general Chen Xianda. All editions read "eighth month" for "eight days"; the Cefu yuansgui, juan 398
translations.idiomatic: Your servant at Pengcheng sent a separate commander who in eight days [reached] Suikou to intercept the rebel general Chen Xianda. All editions read "eighth month" for "eight days"; the Cefu yuansgui, juan 398

sentences.zh: 〈四七三六頁〉
作「八日」。

translations.literal: reads "eight days."
translations.idiomatic: The text reads "eight days."

sentences.zh: 按上云尉元於六月上表，豈得敍八月事。

translations.literal: Since the memorial above places Wei Yuan in the sixth month, how could the eighth month be narrated here? "Month" is corrupt; emend accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: the sixth-month memorial cannot be followed by an eighth-month narrative; "month" is a scribal error.

sentences.zh: 「月」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: "Month" is corrupt; we emend according to the Cefu.
translations.idiomatic: "Month" is corrupt; we emend according to the Cefu.

sentences.zh: 將軍 冊府

translations.literal: General. Cefu
translations.idiomatic: General. Cefu

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈same fascicle and page〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Same fascicle and page.〉

translations.literal: reads "staff" for "army."
translations.idiomatic: The text reads "staff" for "army."

sentences.zh: 按「將軍」謂此白頭翁率領一批軍士，然統觀此段，似只一人。

translations.literal: "General" means this white-haired old man led a body of troops; yet surveying the passage, there seems to be only one man.
translations.idiomatic: "General" means this white-haired old man led a body of troops; yet surveying the passage, there seems to be only one man.

sentences.zh: 「將杖」猶言「持杖」，疑是。

translations.literal: "Wielding a staff" is like "holding a staff"—possibly correct.
translations.idiomatic: "Wielding a staff" is like "holding a staff"—possibly correct.

sentences.zh: 此「將軍」乃因舊本與次行「語汝將軍」相並而訛。

translations.literal: This "general" may be corrupt through juxtaposition with the following line "tell your general."
translations.idiomatic: This "general" may be corrupt through juxtaposition with the following line "tell your general."

sentences.zh: 下邳城我當驅出 冊府

translations.literal: I shall drive Xiapi city out. Cefu
translations.idiomatic: I shall drive Xiapi city out. Cefu

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈same fascicle and page〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Same fascicle and page.〉

sentences.zh: 「城」下有「賊」字。

translations.literal: After "city" there is the character "rebel."
translations.idiomatic: After "city" there is the character "rebel."

sentences.zh: 按無「賊」字較晦，疑當有此字。

translations.literal: Without "rebel" the sense is obscure; the character probably belongs.
translations.idiomatic: Without "rebel" the sense is obscure; the character probably belongs.

sentences.zh: 河內人張超於壞樓所城北故佛圖處獲玉印以獻 冊府卷二三

translations.literal: Henei man Zhang Chao at the ruined fort north of the old pagoda in the city captured a jade seal and presented it. Zizhi tongjian juan 23, p. 246; juan 79, p. 917 read "Huailou New City" for "ruined fort."
translations.idiomatic: Collation on Zhang Chao's jade seal: Zizhi tongjian reads "Huailou New City" where the text has "ruined fort."

sentences.zh: 〈二四六頁〉、

translations.idiomatic: 〈Page 246.〉

sentences.zh: 卷七九

translations.literal: fascicle 79
translations.idiomatic: Fascicle 79.

sentences.zh: 〈九一七頁〉

translations.idiomatic: 〈Page 917.〉

sentences.zh: 「壞樓所城」作「懷樓新城」。

translations.literal: reads "Huai fortress new city" for "ruined fort city."
translations.idiomatic: The text reads "Huai fortress new city" for "ruined fort city."

sentences.zh: 按一０六上地形志上河內是懷州屬郡，懷州武德郡有懷縣，這裏「壞」當是「懷」之訛，指懷縣。

translations.literal: Henei was a commandery of Huai Prefecture in the Geography, juan 106a; Wude Commandery of Huai Prefecture had Huai County; the Geography notes "there is Huai city" for moved seats—here "ruined" is likely "Huai," the county of Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: "ruined" likely stands for Huai County in Huai Prefecture per the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 地形志於懷縣下云「有懷城」，志例，已遷治者，稱「有某城」，皆指故城，可知當時懷遷治新城。

translations.literal: The Geography under Huai County notes "there is Huai city"; by the gazetteer's rule, for relocated seats it says "there is such-and-such city," always meaning the old city—showing that Huai had moved to a new seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Geography under Huai County notes "there is Huai city"; by the gazetteer's rule, for relocated seats it says "there is such-and-such city," always meaning the old city—showing that Huai had moved to a new seat.

sentences.zh: 冊府作「新城」當是。

translations.literal: The Cefu's "new city" is probably correct.
translations.idiomatic: The Cefu's "new city" is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 但「樓」字不可解，疑亦字訛。

translations.literal: But the character "lou" is inexplicable—probably also corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: the character "lou" is unexplained and probably corrupt.

sentences.zh: 貌州上言木連理生於河內之沁縣 按卷一０六上地形志上懷州河內郡有沁水縣。

translations.literal: Memorial that intertwined trees grew in Qin County of Henei. Commentary: per Geography 106a, Huai Prefecture's Henei Commandery had Qinshui County.
translations.idiomatic: Collation on Qin County, Henei: the geography treatise lists Qinshui County under Henei in Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 懷州未置前，此縣當屬豫州。

translations.literal: Before Huai Prefecture was established, this county belonged to Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: before Huai Prefecture existed, the county was under Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 據水經注卷九沁水篇，亦作「沁水城」，疑這裏「沁」下脫「水」字。

translations.literal: According to the Commentary on the Water Classic, juan 9, Qinshui section, it is also "Qinshui city"; suspect here the character "water" is omitted after "Qin."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: the Water Classic commentary reads "Qinshui city"; "water" may be omitted after "Qin" here.
